output.businessUnderstanding: The pipeline correctly identified Imvusa Furniture as a real South African custom furniture, reupholstery, and interior services business operating from two physical locations (George and Bloemfontein), not an ecommerce retailer. It recognized that the absence of shop/cart/checkout/pricing pages is appropriate and expected for a custom-quote services business rather than a defect to fix, and it correctly identified the business's fabric supplier partnership (Hertex Fabrics) and named fabric collections (ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE) as real content to preserve and correct, not invent.
audienceInferred: Homeowners in George, South Africa seeking custom furniture or reupholstery
Homeowners in Bloemfontein, South Africa seeking custom furniture or reupholstery
Interior design-conscious clients wanting curtains, headboards, scatter cushions, wallpaper, or ottomans made to order
Existing or prospective clients of the Hertex Fabrics partnership choosing fabric collections ahead of a project
Local/regional customers who prefer to visit or call a physical studio rather than transact online
output.conversionModelInferred: Lead-generation / consultation model: the site's core conversion action is a prospective client submitting a quote or consultation request (or calling/visiting a location), not completing an online purchase. The blueprint formalizes this into a single canonical conversion funnel (a dedicated Get a Quote flow) fed from Services, Gallery, and Leather Couches pages, backed by one authoritative Contact Block per location — appropriate for custom, individually-quoted work with no published pricing.

siteStrengths.finding: Homepage hero and service cards clearly communicate the full value proposition and service range with concise descriptions.
siteStrengths.evidence: Research report: 'Homepage hero and service cards communicate the value proposition and full service list clearly, each with 1-2 sentence descriptions.'

siteStrengths.finding: Site clearly establishes a genuine two-location presence (George and Bloemfontein), which is real, verifiable business structure worth preserving.
siteStrengths.evidence: Research report business context: 'Two physical locations: George and Bloemfontein.'

siteStrengths.finding: Absence of shop/cart/pricing pages is correctly recognized as appropriate for a custom-quote business model rather than a gap.
siteStrengths.evidence: Research report: 'No pricing is published anywhere on the site - this is expected and appropriate for a custom-quote service business model, not a defect.'

siteStrengths.finding: Site names a real fabric supplier partnership and specific named collections, giving concrete, non-generic content to build on.
siteStrengths.evidence: Research report: 'Site names a fabric supplier partner (Hertex/Hertext Fabrics) and promotes 4 named fabric collections: ADORN, CAPPADOCIA, COASTLINES, ESQUIRE.'

siteStrengths.finding: Existing navigation is simple and shallow, which the blueprint preserves rather than needlessly complicating.
siteStrengths.evidence: Research report: 'Main nav consists of: Home, Leather Couches, Gallery, Services, Contact Us.'

siteStrengths.finding: Not all contact data is broken — email addresses and the Bloemfontein phone number are consistent across pages, showing the underlying data isn't wholesale unreliable.
siteStrengths.evidence: Research report: 'Email addresses ... and Bloemfontein phone (082 824 9790) are consistent between homepage and Contact Us page.'

uxWeaknesses.finding: Prior to the blueprint's redesign, there was no dedicated, structured quote-request flow — CTAs were generic 'contact us' messaging scattered across pages rather than one funnel.
uxWeaknesses.evidence: Site blueprint: replaces 'generic contact us for a quote scattered messaging with one clear funnel' via new /get-a-quote page.

uxWeaknesses.finding: Leather Couches and Gallery pages function as image-only walls with minimal or no supporting text, offering visitors no editorial context, process information, or trust-building narrative.
uxWeaknesses.evidence: Research report: Leather Couches has 'minimal extractable text (heading + one sentence)'; Gallery has 'minimal extractable text (heading only)' and 'appears to be a predominantly image-based portfolio.'

uxWeaknesses.finding: No About/Our Story page exists in current nav, missing an opportunity to build trust for a relationship-driven, consultation-based business.
uxWeaknesses.evidence: Site blueprint: 'About Imvusa' page justified as 'the absence of any about content in the current nav.'

visualWeaknesses.finding: No real visual/design review of the current site has occurred — the proposed design system is an unverified hypothesis with no access to actual site photography, logo, or brand assets.
visualWeaknesses.evidence: Design system explicit DISCLOSURE: 'I have not seen and cannot see the actual Imvusa site, its leather couch photography, gallery images, or any real brand assets... Everything below is a proposed starting hypothesis.'

visualWeaknesses.finding: Leather Couches and Gallery pages could not be assessed for layout quality, image quality, or embedded text-in-image content via text extraction, leaving visual quality genuinely unknown.
visualWeaknesses.evidence: Research report: 'further content, layout quality, or any embedded information in image form could not be assessed via text extraction and requires a real visual/design review.'

visualWeaknesses.finding: All proposed palette and typography tokens are placeholder hypotheses (e.g. saddle-leather brown, terracotta CTA) not yet checked against any real brand colors or existing materials.
visualWeaknesses.evidence: Design system palette entries each marked '(PROPOSED - verify)', e.g. color.brand.primary '#6B3F2A (PROPOSED - verify against real leather/wood tones in photography)'.

seoContentWeaknesses.finding: The Services page contains the entire 8-item services list duplicated back-to-back with identical text, a content-authoring/template error that harms crawl and index clarity.
seoContentWeaknesses.evidence: Research report: 'The Services page contains the entire 8-item services card list duplicated twice in sequence... Content pack notes this was 'actively harming this page's crawl/index clarity.'

seoContentWeaknesses.finding: The fabric supplier's brand name is spelled inconsistently on the same page ('Hertext Fabrics' in intro copy vs 'Hertex' in the CTA), which is unprofessional and dilutes topical/brand relevance.
seoContentWeaknesses.evidence: Research report: 'the Services page intro copy names the fabric supplier Hertext Fabrics but the same page's closing CTA reads More Fabrics at Hertex.'

seoContentWeaknesses.finding: Leather Couches and Gallery pages are thin on indexable text, offering search engines little real content to rank despite being potentially high-intent pages.
seoContentWeaknesses.evidence: Content pack: Leather Couches is 'elevated from a thin, image-only page to a substantive flagship service/editorial page'; Gallery targets 'portfolio/proof-of-work intent' via captioned entries 'instead of an unlabeled image wall.'

seoContentWeaknesses.finding: Inconsistent NAP (Name/Address/Phone) data across pages for two locations undermines local SEO consistency, which search engines weight heavily for multi-location businesses.
seoContentWeaknesses.evidence: Content pack: Contact Us page is positioned as 'the single source of truth for NAP data... this directly resolves the two data mismatches found in research (George phone, Bloemfontein address) and supports local SEO consistency.'

technicalFindings.finding: George office phone number differs between the homepage (082 468 8898) and the Contact Us page (051 430 9883) — a directly observed, unresolved data conflict.
technicalFindings.evidence: Research report: 'Homepage lists George office phone as 082 468 8898; Contact Us page lists George office phone as 051 430 9883.'

technicalFindings.finding: Bloemfontein office address differs between the homepage ('15A Kraal Street, Old East End') and Contact Us page ('6 Alpha Straat, Ou Oos Einde') — a directly observed, unresolved data conflict.
technicalFindings.evidence: Research report: 'Homepage lists Bloemfontein address as 15A Kraal Street, Old East End; Contact Us page lists Bloemfontein address as 6 Alpha Straat, Ou Oos Einde.'

technicalFindings.finding: An inline image CAPTCHA appearing as extracted plain text on both Home ('select the cup') and Contact Us ('select the heart'), flagged in research as a security/accessibility concern, was never mentioned again in blueprint, design system, content pack, or build plan — it was silently dropped rather than ticketed or explicitly deferred.
technicalFindings.evidence: QA report defect P1: 'research_report explicitly flags an inline image CAPTCHA... Neither site_blueprint, design_system, content_pack, nor build_plan mention CAPTCHA... it has simply disappeared from the pipeline.'

technicalFindings.finding: content_pack and build_plan were only supplied as truncated previews, so QA could not fully verify that no page re-authors contact details outside the canonical Contact Block, or confirm full-document consistency.
technicalFindings.evidence: QA report defect P1: 'content_pack v1 content field is marked _truncated:true with only a preview string provided; build_plan v1 content field is likewise marked _truncated:true.'

technicalFindings.finding: Build plan correctly creates two AMBER-gated, blocked tickets refusing to guess between conflicting George phone numbers and Bloemfontein addresses, rather than silently picking one.
technicalFindings.evidence: Build plan tickets 'Fix George Phone Number Mismatch' and 'Fix Bloemfontein Address Mismatch', both flagged 'Do not guess or select between the two conflicting... found in research.'

technicalFindings.finding: Blueprint and build plan add net-new pages (Get a Quote, About, Fabrics & Collections, location subpages) beyond the five pages research actually audited, without a visible record of explicit human sign-off treating this as approved scope.
technicalFindings.evidence: QA report defect P2: 'site_blueprint and build_plan add Get a Quote, About Imvusa, Fabrics & Collections, /contact/george, /contact/bloemfontein as new pages... there is no visible record of human sign-off.'

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Obtain human/client confirmation of the correct George office phone number before entering any value into the canonical Contact Block.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: Build plan ticket 'Fix George Phone Number Mismatch — Single Source of Truth' is explicitly blocked pending human confirmation and must not be guessed; this is a P0 QA-flagged launch blocker.

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Obtain human/client confirmation of the correct Bloemfontein office address before entering any value into the canonical Contact Block.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: Build plan ticket 'Fix Bloemfontein Address Mismatch — Single Source of Truth' is explicitly blocked pending human confirmation and must not be guessed; this is a P0 QA-flagged launch blocker.

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Reintroduce the dropped CAPTCHA/accessibility-security finding as an explicit ticket or documented deferral before proceeding further.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: QA defect P1 found this Stage 1 finding was silently dropped from every downstream artifact rather than carried forward or explicitly deferred with rationale.

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Obtain full (non-truncated) content_pack and build_plan bodies and re-verify that no page re-authors contact details outside the single canonical Contact Block.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: QA defect P1: truncated artifacts prevented certifying that the 'one authoritative contact block' claim holds across every page instance.

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Build the Canonical Contact Block global Elementor template and route Home, Contact Us, and location subpages through it, per build_plan.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: This is the structural fix that, once real data is confirmed, permanently eliminates the phone/address mismatch class of defect.

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Implement the single-authoritative Services list (8 items, no duplication) and standardize fabric supplier spelling to 'Hertex Fabrics' site-wide.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: Directly resolves two content-quality/SEO defects found in research and addressed in content_pack and build_plan.

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Secure explicit human/client sign-off on the net-new page scope (Get a Quote, About, Fabrics & Collections, location subpages) at HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL rather than treating it as pre-approved.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: QA defect P2: scope expansion beyond the five originally audited pages lacks a visible approval trace.

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Commission a real human visual/design review of the Leather Couches and Gallery pages and of all proposed design_system palette/typography tokens against actual site photography and any existing brand assets.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: Design system is explicitly disclosed as an unverified hypothesis with no browsing/image-analysis input; Leather Couches and Gallery could not be assessed via text extraction alone.

recommendedImplementationPlan.step: Proceed through PREVIEW, QA, FINAL REGRESSION AUDIT, and CONTROLLED ACTIVATION TESTING only after the P0 contact-data holds are cleared, then bring to HUMAN LAUNCH APPROVAL as a recorded decision.
recommendedImplementationPlan.rationale: Doctrine: launch never auto-approves; QA-clean is necessary but not sufficient, and open holds (contact data) must be a deliberate recorded human decision if launched with them still open.

unsupportedAssumptionsRejected: QA rejected the implicit assumption that content_pack and build_plan's claim of 'a single canonical contact block used identically everywhere' could be treated as fully verified — flagged as a material verification gap because both artifacts were only supplied truncated.

QA rejected the assumption that the CAPTCHA/accessibility-security risk raised in Stage 1 could be considered resolved or safely out of scope simply because later stages did not mention it — treated as a silently dropped issue requiring explicit re-ticketing or documented deferral, not a clean pass.

QA rejected the assumption that adding net-new pages (Get a Quote, About, Fabrics & Collections, location subpages) beyond the five originally audited pages is automatically approved scope just because it was framed as blueprint-justified — required explicit human sign-off traceability instead.

QA rejected treating the two AMBER-blocked contact-data tickets as resolved or launch-ready on paper — explicitly reaffirmed these remain a P0 real-world fact gap that cannot be cleared by any pipeline stage without human/client confirmation.

Which Bloemfontein office address is actually correct: '15A Kraal Street, Old East End' (homepage) or '6 Alpha Straat, Ou Oos Einde' (Contact Us page) — or has the office moved and both are stale?
Is the fabric supplier's correct brand name 'Hertex Fabrics' or 'Hertext Fabrics' — has this been confirmed directly with the supplier/client rather than assumed from majority usage?

Should the previously flagged inline image CAPTCHA (differing prompts on Home vs Contact Us, appearing as plain extracted text) be investigated now as a security/accessibility issue, or explicitly deferred to a later phase with documented rationale?

Does the client approve the blueprint's added pages (Get a Quote, About Imvusa, Fabrics & Collections, /contact/george, /contact/bloemfontein) as in-scope, or should the rebuild stay strictly limited to the five originally audited pages?
Can the client supply the full, non-truncated content_pack and build_plan documents so a complete consistency check can be performed before HUMAN DESIGN APPROVAL?

Are there any existing brand guidelines, logo files, or real site photography available so the proposed (currently unverified) design_system palette and typography can be checked against actual brand assets rather than treated as a blind hypothesis?
